title: One sidebar, every session
description: Session cards are the single switcher: drag to reorder, pin, duplicate, split into the grid, or tear off into a new window. An unread dot tells you the moment an agent needs you.

title: Up to 8 sessions on screen
description: A smart grid with selectable layouts and mixable agents per cell. Your manual layout pick sticks until the grid is actually full; arrow keys move focus.

title: A worktree per session
description: Spin up a git worktree from the new-session dialog, and choose merge, squash, or discard when the session closes. The branch chip always shows where you are.

title: Review work hunk by hunk
description: A verified review cockpit for agent output: stage individual hunks, accept or reject at diff level, and group related changes into changelists.

title: Setups you save once
description: Profiles carry a working directory, per-agent arguments, and env vars. They are agent-agnostic: Claude-only flags are stripped automatically when another agent launches.

title: Close the app, keep the conversation
description: Sessions are re-attached by id on restart, so a Claude Code conversation survives a reboot. Save a named workspace to restore a whole layout at once.

title: F1 for everything
description: A command palette for actions, F2 for session history, and a full keyboard map underneath. Built for people who never touch the mouse.

title: Native by construction
description: Tauri and Rust, not Electron. A small signed binary with real PTYs, SQLite storage, desktop notifications, and auto-updates from GitHub releases.
